messages:
infra-oncall: 🚨 apac2 control plane auth failing — console throwing 401s, config rollouts blocked, and routing agent reporting degraded rules. GPU scheduler shows ~50% unschedulable on apac2-gpu pools. Investigating now.

deploy-bot: [alert] control-plane-apac2: auth-errs spike 2025-10-11T09:20Z — linked: https://internal/alerts/2345 :rotating_light:

sophie: copying — seeing `403` from /v1/configs on the control plane from the rollback worker. Console loads but then 401 on any protected route.

ajay: @sophie can you paste the control-plane logs for auth proxy? I want the initial error type (token validation vs cert).

sophie: sure — tail from auth-proxy: 
```
2025-10-11T09:19:03Z auth-proxy ERROR validate_token failed: upstream: dial tcp 10.12.5.9:443: connect: network unreachable
2025-10-11T09:19:04Z auth-proxy ERROR fallback jwt verify failed: no keys
```

leo: network unreachable to KMS endpoints in apac2? That would break token introspection. @maria any infra changes rolled in last hour?

maria: just a routine routing config push to the regional edge — nothing to KMS. But I do see the control-plane nodes in apac2 have flapped BGP sessions to the transit peers around 09:18Z.

infra-oncall: ok hypothesis: upstream network flap to KMS/identity service causing auth failures which then cause control plane to mark many nodes unhealthy -> scheduler reports GPUs unschedulable. Plan: 1) short circuit console / control plane auth checks for critical ops to allow rollbacks (temp allowlist), 2) shift traffic away from apac2 routing policies to west1 for customer-facing lanes, 3) start on-demand GPU nodes in west1 to absorb workload.

ajay: +1 on shifting. I'll open a routing override: set `region_priority: [west1,eu1,apac2]` and lower apac2 weight to 0. Doing now.

leo: FYI changing routing weight will cause extra cross-region egress. Cost estimate: ~3-5k USD/day at current traffic if we keep west1 absorbing. We should cap burst to essential routes only.

maria: starting on-demand GPU instances in west1 (p3-equivalent) — will be ready in ~12m. If we spin up autoscaling groups please note reserved capacity won't apply.

infra-oncall: executing temporary allowlist for rollout/rollback APIs for infra team only. Command: 
```
curl -X POST https://control.api.internal/v1/ops/allowlist -d '{"users":["infra-oncall","sophie","ajay","maria"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

sophie: allowlist applied, can confirm /v1/configs now returns 200 for infra tokens. Starting blocked rollouts now.

maria: BGP sessions on the affected transit are still noisy. Net team engaging with carrier — they see flaps due to a blade in the provider ASM. ETA for hardware swap ~45m per carrier.

ops-bot: [status update] routing override applied, on-demand GPU ASG started in west1 (3 nodes requested) — health checking.

ajay: traffic shift looks stable from metrics side. Console still 401 for most orgs (public tokens) — those will remain affected until carrier fix or we proxy auth to eu1 KMS which is riskier. Recommendation: message CSE to throttle noncritical jobs and enable emergency fallback docs.

leo: cost cap in place: emergency egress budget set to $4k/day; if exceeded auto-scale will stop. Not ideal but prevents runaway spend.

infra-oncall: agreed. Maria, keep carrier ticket open. Sophie, coordinate with CSE to throttle training jobs and inform affected customers. Ajay, leave routing override active until control plane auth stable and apac2 BGP steady for 30m.

maria: carrier acknowledges hardware replacement; tech onsite ETA 40m.

sophie: pinged CSE + sent draft incident banner for console: "Console and config rollouts degraded in apac2 due to regional control plane networking issue; failover to west1 in progress. " Will post after infra confirms.

infra-oncall: logging incident, assigning Sev2. Will follow up with a short postmortem once carrier confirm and we have timeline. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
